tier_reason: Lowered C to D: after the enricher's pass there is still no ratio against any baseline anywhere reachable. The repo ships the harness (bench.sh, test.c, Makefile with gcc -O2) but no results; the only figures are search snippets of the author's blocked 2019 blog post, which give absolute throughput (about 5.3 Gpx/s on 8 threads for a 16383x16383 downscale) and directional statements (Pixman the fastest single-threaded competitor at 0.5-1.0x, Skia among the fastest at under 0.5x; libswscale and stb_image_resize not in the published comparison). Those figures are also for the 2019 code, before the 2023 rewrite. Directional evidence without a reproducible number is D.

corrections.claimed_speedup: No ratio against any baseline is reachable. Search snippets of the author's blocked 2019 post 'Battle of the Bilerps' give absolute throughput only (about 5.3 Gpx/s, roughly 21 GB/s of input, on 8 threads of an i7-4770K for a 16383x16383 downscale) and directional statements (Pixman the fastest single-threaded competitor at 0.5-1.0x of Smolscale's speed, Skia below 0.5x); libswscale and stb_image_resize are not in the published comparison. The figures predate the 2023 rewrite.
corrections.caveats: Snippet-only, directional, and for the 2019 code before the 2023 rewrite. The README is stale (the build needs smolscale-generic.c; the AVX2 file has about 278 _mm256 uses). No allocation or argument checks (a zero dimension divides by zero). The harness times sws_getContext inside each call and bundles stb_image_resize v0.97. The Chafa copy is maintained but has an incompatible API.
